conventions.convention: Backgrounds use finite G, finite additive abelian A, a left action ρ, and a normalized 3-cocycle β. Coefficients reside at the first vertex; δ_a B = a*β. The skeletal associator runs from (gh)k to g(hk).
Raw vertex/edge gauge labels remain distinct even when their effects on backgrounds coincide. A 2-arrow satisfies λ′−λ = δ_b t; horizontal composition is s+ρ_h t and the associator is β(k_i,h_i,g_i).

The physical interface uses finite configuration sets on a finite ordered triangulation of a closed compact oriented smooth manifold, with a specified tangential lift held fixed under internal gauge arrows.

Correlators are unnormalized finite sums with W_x = μ_x exp(−S_x); the empty insertion tuple gives Z_x. Natural units c = ℏ = 1 are used, and background labels, action phases and partition weights are dimensionless.

A coherent phase is adopted model data, equals 1 on identity arrows, multiplies under composition and agrees on 2-isomorphic arrows. Permitted local counterterms change it by exp(iL_y)χ_f exp(−iL_x). Postnikov data do not themselves specify this phase.
The singleton examples specify background-response functors only and expressly do not construct an effective nontrivial physical symmetry realization.

load_bearing.statement: A finite 2-group background coupling is a pseudofunctor F: B(K) → M, with the explicitly specified finite model fibers, gauge transports, comparison and unit maps, coherence equations, complete insertion transports, and separately adopted weight transformation laws.

Under the stated finite configuration, bijective transport, observable covariance and coherent configuration-independent phase hypotheses, C_y(α_f O_1,…,α_f O_n) = χ_f(x) C_x(O_1,…,O_n) and Z_y = χ_f(x) Z_x. An allowed counterterm changes the phase to exp(iL_y)χ_f(x)exp(−iL_x).

concerns.concern: The Statement says that the phase “is determined by the selected model's action and measure.” This needs the qualification already present in the defining supplier: when W_x is identically zero, including an empty configuration fiber, the weight equation does not determine χ_f uniquely. The theorem explicitly adopts a model-specified coherent phase, so its finite-sum identities remain valid; the concluding determination wording should retain that distinction.
